title: Faith That Moves Mountains
subtitle: The smallest seed in the story is the point of the story.
objectives: State Hebrews 11:1 and explain what it defines
Explain the mustard seed image in Matthew 17:20
Explain why the size of the faith is not the point
Give an example of faith shown by action

cards.title: The verse everybody quotes is about size
cards.text: Faith the size of a mustard seed, and you could tell this mountain to move. Matthew 17, verse 20.

cards.title: The definition the Bible gives
cards.text: Faith is confidence in what is hoped for, and assurance about what is not seen. It is a definition, not a feeling.
points: **"What is hoped for"** — it points forward.
**"Not seen"** — evidence has not arrived yet.
**It is about acting** before the proof does.
**Hebrews 11 then lists people** who did exactly that.

cards.title: Why a mustard seed
cards.text: It was the smallest seed anyone in that audience planted. The comparison is deliberate and it is about size.
points: **About a millimetre across.**
**Everybody listening had seen one.**
**The point is that a small amount is enough.**
**Not that you need more of it.**

question.text: What does Hebrews 11:1 say faith is?
options: Confidence in what is hoped for and assurance about what is not seen
question.explain: It is given as a definition. Faith points forward, before the evidence has arrived.

cards.title: Small and repeated is how anything grows
cards.text: A seed does nothing visible for days. Then it does everything. That is not a metaphor about seeds; it is how seeds work.
points: **Nothing happens, and then a lot happens.**
**Bone, muscle and skill** all behave this way.
**Most people quit** during the invisible part.
**Small is not the same as weak.**

question.text: Why is a mustard seed used in the comparison?
options: It was the smallest seed the audience knew
It was the most expensive seed
It was the only seed grown there
question.explain: The smallness is the whole point. A small amount is enough, and more is not the requirement.

cards.title: Good spot to pause
cards.text: Part 2 is the difference between faith and wishing, which is where the passage gets misread. Your place is saved.

cards.title: Faith is not the same as wanting something badly
cards.text: This is the misreading the verse gets most often, and it turns a promise into a test you cannot pass.

cards.title: Wishing sits still. Faith moves
cards.text: Every example in Hebrews 11 is someone doing something. None of them is someone hoping harder.
points: **Noah built.** Abraham left. Moses went back.
**Wishing is a feeling you hold.**
**Faith is a thing you then do.**
**James 2:17** — faith without action is dead.

cards.title: Every character is judged on what they do
cards.text: In a story, someone who says they are brave and never acts is not brave. Nobody has to explain that rule to a reader.
points: **Action reveals what a character actually believes.**
**That is why Hebrews 11 is a list of deeds.**
**Not a list of feelings.**
**Same rule** in anything you write.

question.text: What is the difference between faith and wishing?
options: Faith results in action; wishing stays a feeling
question.explain: Every example in Hebrews 11 is someone who did something. James 2:17 says the same plainly.

cards.title: What the mountain stands for
cards.text: Nobody in the passage relocates a physical mountain. It is the standard image for something immovable.
points: **Something too big to shift** by ordinary effort.
**The claim is about what becomes possible**, not geology.
**Read it as an exam, a habit, a fear.**
**Those are the mountains you actually have.**

cards.title: Nobody talks themselves into being ready
cards.text: Confidence before a fight does not come from wanting it. It comes from the rounds already done, weeks earlier.
points: **Belief follows the work.** Not the other way round.
**Small sessions, repeated**, become certainty.
**The seed, again.**
**You cannot feel your way to prepared.**

question.text: Matthew 17:20 says you need a large amount of faith to see anything happen.
question.explain: False. It says the opposite. A mustard seed's worth is enough, and its smallness is the point.

terms.def: Confidence in what is hoped for, assurance about what is not seen. Hebrews 11:1.
The chapter that defines faith and then lists people who acted on it.
The smallest seed the original audience knew. Used to say a small amount is enough.
Faith the size of a mustard seed could tell a mountain to move.
Faith without action is dead. The clearest statement of the difference from wishing.
In this image, anything too big to move by ordinary effort.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Hebrews 11:1** — confidence in what is not yet seen.
**A mustard seed is enough.** Smallness is the point.
**Faith acts. Wishing sits still.**
**The mountain is whatever will not move for you.**

options: Confidence in what is hoped for, assurance about what is not seen

Believing without any reason at all

quiz.text: Put the argument of the lesson in order.
items: Faith is assurance about what is not seen
A mustard seed's worth is enough
Faith shows itself in action, not feeling
The mountain is whatever will not move for you
quiz.explain: Definition, then size, then action, then application. That is the shape of the whole lesson.

teacher.summary: Week 3 Devotion covers faith, matching the Term 1 theme. The lesson is organised around two corrections, because both misreadings are common and both are discouraging. The first is that the mustard seed verse is about needing more faith, when the passage says a very small amount is enough — the smallness is the argument. The second is that faith means wanting something strongly, which turns the verse into a test nobody can pass; the lesson answers it with Hebrews 11, which is a list of things people did, and James 2:17. The mountain is explained as the standard image for the immovable rather than as geology, so that the promise can be applied to an exam or a habit rather than dismissed.
discussion: Ask him what his mountain is at the moment. The answer makes the passage concrete rather than abstract.
Ask why the seed is small rather than large in the comparison. Getting to 'a small amount is enough' is the whole first half.
Ask what the difference is between believing you can do something and doing it. James 2:17 is the short version.
Ask what happens during the part of growth where nothing is visible. It is the same question for a seed, a skill and a habit.
teacher.extension: Have him write down one thing he has been hoping about, and one action that would count as faith rather than wishing about it. Two lines, and the second one is the point.
misconceptions: 'The verse means you need a lot of faith.' It says a mustard seed's worth is enough. The smallness is the argument.
'Faith means wanting something badly.' Hebrews 11 is a list of things people did, not of feelings they had.
'Moving mountains means literal mountains.' It is the standard image for something that will not shift by ordinary effort.
'Faith means being certain.' Hebrews 11:1 describes assurance about what is not seen. Certainty would need no faith.
